package_info.why_malicious: The Log4j package contains a severe zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228) that allows remote code execution when processing specially crafted log messages. This enables attackers to execute arbitrary code on servers using vulnerable versions, leading to full system compromise.

execution_context.file_location: application log statements processed by Log4j (core logging logic)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed, Log4j performs a remote JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled LDAP server, retrieves and executes remote code, resulting in arbitrary code execution on the vulnerable server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows untrusted user input in log messages to trigger remote code execution via JNDI lookups, which is highly dangerous and not expected in normal logging operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging libraries should never execute code or perform network lookups based on log message content. Here, user-controlled input leads to code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups are sometimes used for legitimate resource resolution in trusted, internal environments, but never with untrusted user input.
key_indicators: Presence of ${jndi:...} patterns in log messages
Log4j performing outbound LDAP/RMI lookups at runtime
Unexpected code execution triggered by log input

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern to a vulnerable server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Log4j processes the log message and initiates a remote JNDI lookup.

attack_chain.action: Log4j performs a remote JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled LDAP server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code is retrieved and executed on the vulnerable server, leading to full compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Log4j processing log messages containing ${jndi:...} patterns
Unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI/DNS network requests from application servers
Runtime code execution triggered by log input
file_indicators: Presence of log4j-core-2.x.jar in application dependencies
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP/RMI/DNS requests to external, untrusted domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for ${jndi:...} patterns, inspect network traffic for unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI/DNS requests, and audit dependencies for vulnerable Log4j versions. Use IPS/IDS signatures to detect exploit attempts and block suspicious JNDI lookups.
